statement: Recent-graduate unemployment minus the all-worker rate >= 2.0 pp in any 2027 quarter (NY Fed College Labor Market, 2027 quarterly)
status_at_phase_end: Gap elevated but below threshold throughout 2026: ~1.5-1.6 pp in Q1-Q2, narrowing to ~1.2 pp in Q3 (5.2% vs 4.0%). 2026 year-to-date average ~1.4 pp, reported as the widest adverse gap in the series. Underemployment rose to 42.5% (highest since Oct 2020).

items.summary: Regional central bank's quarterly update with 2025:Q4 data: recent-graduate (22-27) unemployment ~5.6% in December 2025; October 2025 values estimated because of missing survey data.
items.detail: NY Fed 'Labor Market for Recent College Graduates', release 2026-02-04 (data through 2025:Q4). December figure per Bloomberg (2026-05-05). All-worker rate for Dec 2025 not verified; gap roughly 1.3-1.5 pp.

items.summary: 2026:Q1 update: recent-graduate unemployment 'remained elevated at about 5.7%' in Q1 (5.6% in March); young non-graduates fell to 7.2% from 7.7%. Gap vs all workers ~1.5 pp.
items.detail: NY Fed post on X/Facebook 2026-05-05; Bloomberg 'Unemployment for Recent College Grads Remains High' 2026-05-05.

items.summary: Labour think-tank analysis: young college-graduate unemployment rose from 4.0% (Jul 2023) to 5.3% (Mar 2026), 1.0 pp above the overall rate, but mostly because of higher participation; the graduate employment-to-population ratio has held steady since 2024.
items.detail: Economic Policy Institute, 'Class of 2026: Young college graduates face a weaker labor market...' (EPI's own CPS definition, differs from NY Fed). Date approximate (spring 2026).

items.summary: 2026:Q2 update: recent-graduate unemployment ~5.6% (Q2 average; 5.7% in June) vs 4.1% for all workers - a gap of ~1.5-1.6 pp, the highest Q2 graduate rate since 2013 excluding 2020-21; underemployment ~42%.
items.detail: NY Fed release 2026-08-06 with 2026:Q2 data; values via careerfirstnexus.com table and NPR (2026-08-18). Q2 2025: 5.3% vs 4.0%.

items.summary: 2026:Q3 update: recent-graduate unemployment fell to 5.2% (lowest in over a year) vs 4.0% for all workers - gap ~1.2 pp, narrowing; underemployment rose to 42.5%, the highest since Oct 2020. 2026 average gap ~1.4 pp, widest adverse gap in the series.
items.detail: NY Fed chart metadata 'November 2, 2026, with 2026:Q3 data'; September 3-month averages: grads 5.2%, all workers 4.0%, young non-grads 7.4% (twin-seeker.com, Bloc A Post 2026-11-02).

items.summary: Series covers Bloc A only; Bloc B publishes urban youth (16-24) unemployment excluding students but no recent-graduate vs all-worker series on a comparable basis.
items.detail: Bloc B NBS youth unemployment (16-24 excl. students) is not graduate-specific; not compared in this run.
